clue.text: Trade TUC misrepresented — giving basis for emotional expression?

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so the letters are presented in a different order

parts.note: taken as written; the TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress

explanation.surface: A union body's account of trade is distorted, prompting an emotional reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: crying is emotional expression, and tears flow from the gland's duct.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeping shows feeling, and the small channel draining tears from the eye is physically where that outward show starts.

clue.text: Test held up silent comedian and actor

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars
Oliver Hardy of Laurel and Hardy, stars of silent film

explanation.surface: An exam was delayed by a comic from the silent era and a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the UK's compulsory yearly vehicle inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Hardy is an English film star known for roles in Mad Max: Fury Road and Inception.

clue.text: Gentleman enthralled by top appointed authority in Indian city

indicators.note: being enthralled by something means being captivated, held within it

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as I
Mr is the title for a man
a tsar is an official appointed by government to oversee a policy area, such as a drugs tsar

explanation.surface: A gentleman captivated by a senior official in a city on the subcontinent.
explanation.walkthrough: A(MR)I then TSAR; A1 is commonly rendered AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Amritsar is a city in Punjab, home of the Golden Temple, the holiest Sikh shrine.

clue.text: Irish writer, mostly respected senior figure penning end to novel

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as animals in a pen, so one piece sits within the other
mostly means not entirely, so the last letter is left off

parts.note: a doyen is the most respected or senior member of a group

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: An Irish author, largely an esteemed elder statesman, at work on the close of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: DOYEN loses its N, then L is penned: DOY(L)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Roddy Doyle is a Booker-winning Dublin novelist, author of The Commitments and Paddy Clarke Ha Ha Ha.

clue.text: Right-wing fellow round movement infused with nationalist hostility

indicators.note: something infused with another has it steeped inside, so the letter sits within the movement

parts.note: short for Conservative
F is the abbreviation for fellow
turning in a circle
N is the abbreviation for nationalist

explanation.surface: A conservative bloke stirring up anti-foreign feeling in a political campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: CON + F + RO(N)TATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A confrontation is a hostile clash or face-off between opposing sides, an open show of antagonism.

clue.text: Unknown character in a run-down district gets place of refuge

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it, so the character goes within the district

parts.note: a slum is a squalid, decaying area of a town
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A mysterious stranger in a deprived neighbourhood finds somewhere to shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The unknown goes inside: A S(Y)LUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or sanctuary granted to someone fleeing danger, hence a safe haven.

clue.text: Group neatly staged rock without label

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so these letters are jolted into a new order
without means lacking, so the letters of the label are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
a tag is a label attached to something

explanation.surface: A band put on a tidy rock show without a record company behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' reads as the band's genre, which suits a group, but it is the anagram signal. Remove T, A and G from the twelve letters before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely Dan is the American jazz-rock band of Walter Becker and Donald Fagen, so a musical group.

clue.text: Bring up trouble about a broadcast medium in European country

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the trouble word goes around the rest
in a down clue, bringing a word up makes it read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
taken as written
television

explanation.surface: Raising a fuss about a television channel somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the trouble word is turned upside down; the rest goes inside it unreversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvia is a Baltic state in northern Europe, between Estonia and Lithuania.

clue.text: Sacrificial figure with extremists in territory taken in by BBC news presenter

indicators.note: being taken in by someone means being absorbed inside, so the pair goes within the presenter's name

parts.note: Andrew Marr, long-time BBC political journalist and presenter

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, so only the first and last are kept

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A victim among militant extremists in occupied land, conned by a BBC newsreader.
explanation.walkthrough: MAR(TY)R: 'extremists' looks like militants but just means the end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr is someone who suffers or dies for a cause or belief, offering up their life.

clue.text: Join family in tram or ground covering yard

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, so the yard sits within the jumble
ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are broken up and remade

parts.note: taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Someone boards a tram, or some turf is laid over a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder; the Y slips into the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To marry into a family is to become part of it through a wedding, joining that household as a relative.

clue.text: Distasteful thing first person on Italian island raised

parts.note: an object is a thing
the first-person pronoun
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it so it reads upwards

parts.note: Elba, Napoleon's island of exile off Tuscany

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant first raised by a person on an Italian island.
explanation.walkthrough: OBJECT + I + ON + ELBA upside down as ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Objectionable means offensive or unpleasant, arousing dislike, which matches distasteful.

clue.text: Record middle of America free of cold

indicators.note: being free of something means being without it, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: the middle spelt the American way
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A record set in the American heartland, somewhere without cold weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of America' is doing double duty as a spelling hint: the US form is CENTER, and removing C leaves ENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data or details is to write them into a register or system, so it means to log.

clue.text: One half of TV duo uncovered, we're told, animal

parts.note: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting pair

indicators.note: something we are told reaches us by ear, so the spoken form matters rather than spelling

parts.note: uncovered means naked; the word for that sounds like the large mammal

explanation.surface: One member of a television double act has been exposed, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant McPartlin and Declan Donnelly are the presenting duo Ant and Dec.
explanation.definitionFit: The antbear is another name for the aardvark, a burrowing African mammal that feeds on termites.

clue.text: What could be inspired in prankish humorist Dom?

definitions.text: What could be inspired in prankish humorist Dom?

indicators.note: placing one thing in another puts it inside, so the first piece goes within the comedian's name

parts.note: Dom Joly is the British comedian behind the hidden-camera show Trigger Happy TV
lit up, fired with excitement

explanation.surface: Asking what feeling a practical joker of a comedian might arouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Dom Joly is known for pranks on Trigger Happy TV; LIT goes inside his surname, JO(LLIT)Y, and the whole clue describes what he aims to provoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Jollity is merriment and cheerful fun, just what a comic's pranks are meant to stir up.

clue.text: Figures in a ring related to an area?

definitions.text: Figures in a ring related to an area?

parts.note: surface reading: shapes or people arranged in a circle, as in a dance or a geometry problem
setter's reading: numbers keyed when making a phone call (a ring), tied to a geographical region

explanation.walkthrough: 'Area' suggests geometry and 'figures in a ring' a circle diagram; in fact a ring is a phone call and the figures are its digits.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional prefix is the group of digits one keys before a local number when telephoning a particular district.

clue.text: Take orders after extended rest and stay hidden ahead?

parts.note: a lie-in is a long stay in bed in the morning
as a waiter does at tables

explanation.surface: A waiter after a long sleep who then keeps out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'stay hidden ahead' describes setting an ambush for someone yet to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to conceal oneself in readiness to ambush someone before they arrive.

clue.text: House in confines of wood trailed by division in crime narrative

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it, so the house goes inside
the confines of something are its boundaries, so only its outer letters are kept

parts.note: its first and last letters
HO is the abbreviation for house
a unit is a section or department

explanation.surface: A house at the edge of a forest followed by an army detachment in a thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: W(HO)D then UNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunit is a detective story centred on discovering who committed the murder.

clue.text: Ghostly sort of crate put in small place

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: being put in something means being placed inside it

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

indicators.note: a sort of thing is a version of it, here read as sorted, the letters reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An eerie box squeezed into a tiny room.
explanation.walkthrough: S + P(ECTRA)L.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectral means relating to a spectre, a phantom or apparition, so it is synonymous with eerie or phantom-like.

clue.text: Affair bringing stories with it

parts.note: relations are accounts or narrations, as in relating a tale
hip means fashionable, up to date

explanation.surface: A love affair that comes with plenty of gossip attached.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a romantic or sexual liaison, which is one kind of bond between two people.

clue.text: A working party announced increase in growth

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a crew is a team assembled to do a job

explanation.surface: A team on a job declares that output is rising.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrue is to accumulate or build up over time, as interest grows in an account.

clue.text: Drunk Greek character given first of strong soluble powder

parts.note: lit is slang for intoxicated
the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, which alone is taken

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: An inebriated Greek fellow handed a strong dissolving powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus is a dye obtained from lichens, sold as a water-soluble powder and used to test acidity.

clue.text: Prominent feature about a container restricted for Italian tipple

indicators.note: about means around, so the facial feature wraps the single letter

parts.note: a jutting part of the face
taken as written

indicators.note: restricted means held short, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a tin is a metal receptacle

explanation.surface: A big nose or chin seen through a wine carafe, perhaps, in an Italian bar.
explanation.walkthrough: CHI(A)N, then TIN loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany, so a typical Italian drink.

clue.text: Negative utterance varied amid hundred of wandering types

parts.note: the word of refusal

indicators.note: varied means altered or changed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A chorus of refusals among a hundred travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amid' looks like a positional word but is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic describes peoples who roam from place to place with no fixed home, the defining trait of wanderers.

clue.text: Some antitheft fences signified

indicators.note: a fence encloses ground, so these words surround the answer within them

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Some security barriers designed to stop stealing mean something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a hidden-word signal for antitheft alone; it is itself part of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant is the past tense of mean, to convey or denote, so it equals indicated.

clue.text: Male in difficulty with a foreign dance

indicators.note: a thing placed in another is enclosed by it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: as in 'there's the rub', a snag
M is the abbreviation for male
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man struggling with an unfamiliar dance step.
explanation.walkthrough: RU(M)B then A.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a ballroom dance of Cuban origin, so it comes from abroad for an English-speaking solver.

clue.text: Wealthy figure, artist, at home with Charles' mother — it entails minimal effort!

parts.note: a nob is a rich or upper-class person
Royal Academician
being in means being at home
Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth II, mother of King Charles III

explanation.surface: A rich man and a painter visit the late Queen at home, and it is no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina, so Charles' mother here.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-brainer is a decision or task so obvious that it requires hardly any thought or work.

clue.text: Fake element in trainers at zoo

indicators.note: an element in something is a part of it, so the answer is a run of letters within the next words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Something phoney about the people who coach animals at the zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an imitation or inferior substitute, so it is synonymous with counterfeit or artificial.

clue.text: A lot trained after time with aid for drivers — like the AA?

parts.note: golfers drive the ball off a tee

indicators.note: trained means drilled or shaped, so these letters are put into new order

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Much training for motorists, overseen by the Automobile Association.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA looks like the British motoring organisation, which fits 'drivers'; here it is Alcoholics Anonymous, and drivers are golfers.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcoholics Anonymous members commit to abstaining entirely from drink, which is what a teetotaller does.
